notes: The tutorial covers many separate circuits (LED, button, buzzer, traffic lights, PIR, ultrasonic, MCP3008, motors). The two supplied images both show only the LDR + capacitor light-sensing circuit, so that is the circuit built here.

Image 1 (Fritzing) shows the Pi rotated 180°: red wire to top-row rightmost pin = physical pin 1 (3V3); green wire to pin 7 (GPIO4, matching LightSensor(4) in the code); black wire to bottom row pin 6 (GND).

Breadboard: wires in row a of columns 1, 3 and 5; LDR across columns 1 and 3 (row e); capacitor across columns 3 (+, long leg, same strip as the LDR leg) and 5 (-). Circuit: 3V3 -> LDR -> GPIO4 node -> capacitor -> GND. Column numbers are read as labelled on the breadboard images (column 1 at the right in image 1).
Breadboard bank/row naming: the components and wires are placed in the top half (rows a-e) as 't' holes.
The capacitor-1uf type is not in the catalogue, so a new part type was added (ports + and -, polarized).
Jumper-wire-mf port 'a' is taken as the male end (into the breadboard) and 'b' as the female end (onto the Pi header pin).
The Pi is matched to rpi-4b; its GPIO header pins are used as ports 3V3, GPIO4 and GND (physical pin 6) even though the catalogue lists only GPIO_HEADER.
The component types and the three wire colours (red, green, black) come from the Fritzing image; the manual does not name them.
